record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Complete in full detail the construction of the three-dimensional Gross-Neveu model with a large number of components, and construct analogous non-renormalizable models such as the corresponding regime of the sine-Gordon model.

evidence.quote: Complete in full detail the construction of the first non renormalizable field theory, the Gross-Neveu model in three dimensions and large number of components [dCFdVMS][dV]. Construct other models of this type, for instance the corresponding regime of the sine-Gordon model.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Provide a complete, fully detailed mathematical construction of the three-dimensional Gross–Neveu model in the regime of a large number of fermionic components, treated as a non-renormalizable Euclidean quantum field theory. Concretely:

1. Let N be a large positive integer, and consider on R^3 an N-component Euclidean Dirac fermion field ψ = (ψ_a)_{a=1,...,N} with formal action
   S(ψ, ψ̄) = ∫_{R^3} ( ψ̄(x) ∂̸ ψ(x) + (g/(2N)) ( ψ̄(x) ψ(x) )^2 ) dx,
where ∂̸ is the Euclidean Dirac operator and g > 0 is a coupling constant. Although the quartic interaction has dimensionful coupling making the model perturbatively non-renormalizable, the 1/N expansion is expected to render it well defined.

Construct, with full mathematical rigor (e.g. using a multi-scale renormalization-group / cluster / Mayer expansion adapted to the 1/N expansion), the infinite-volume Schwinger functions of this model. In particular: define a sequence of ultraviolet- and infrared-cutoff measures, prove convergence (Borel summability or equivalent) of the 1/N expansion of the connected Schwinger functions uniformly in the cutoffs, prove existence and uniqueness of cutoff-removal limits, establish the expected non-perturbative mass generation (dynamical chiral symmetry breaking) and verify the Osterwalder–Schrader axioms in the resulting limit.

2. Carry out an analogous construction for at least one further non-renormalizable Euclidean field theory of the same type. Specifically, in the corresponding non-renormalizable regime of the two-dimensional sine-Gordon model — i.e., the Coulomb-gas regime above the Kosterlitz–Thouless threshold (β^2 > 8π) where the cosine interaction ∫ cos(βφ) becomes non-renormalizable — construct the model rigorously, defining the appropriate cutoff theory, controlling its renormalization, and proving existence of a non-trivial infinite-volume limit with the expected qualitative properties.
artifact.status_search_result: A construction of the 3D Gross–Neveu model at large N was announced and partially carried out by de Calan, Faria da Veiga, Magnen and Sénéor (PRL 1991; Springer Lecture Notes 1995), establishing the framework, mass generation and partial control of the 1/N expansion. However, a fully detailed published construction completing all technical estimates, and analogous constructions for other non-renormalizable models such as the corresponding sine-Gordon regime, do not appear to have been completed in the literature; the problem is therefore best classified as partially solved/still open in its full form.

status_evidence.snippet: de Calan, Faria da Veiga, Magnen, Sénéor: construction of the 3D Gross-Neveu model at large N.
status_evidence.claim: Initial construction of the 3D large-N Gross–Neveu model was carried out, supporting partial-solution status.

status_evidence.title: Mass generation in the large N Gross-Neveu model
status_evidence.snippet: Companion paper proving dynamical mass generation in the large-N 3D Gross-Neveu model.
status_evidence.claim: Dynamical mass generation has been established, but full detailed construction and extensions remain incomplete.
